basic_information.name: No-Code Agent Builders (Lindy, Relevance AI, n8n)
basic_information.creator: Lindy: Lindy.ai Inc. (Flo Crivello, San Francisco, USA, founded Jan 2023); Relevance AI: Relevance AI Pty Ltd (Daniel Vassilev, Jacky Koh, Daniel Palmer, Sydney, Australia, founded 2020); n8n: n8n GmbH (Jan Oberhauser, Berlin, Germany, founded 2019)
basic_information.release_date: Lindy: January 2023 (public launch March 2023 with 70k waitlist signups); Relevance AI: 2020 (pivoted to AI agents ~2023); n8n: October 2019 (first GitHub release June 2019, v1.0 July 2023)
basic_information.license: Lindy: Proprietary (closed-source SaaS); Relevance AI: Proprietary (closed-source SaaS, SDK available on GitHub); n8n: Sustainable Use License (fair-code, source-available but not OSI-approved open source — free self-hosting for internal/non-commercial use, enterprise license for commercial redistribution)
basic_information.current_version: Lindy: Lindy 2.0 (continuously updated SaaS, no public version numbering); Relevance AI: Continuously updated SaaS, no public version numbering; n8n: Actively releasing (latest release ~Feb 2026, continuous updates, 89k+ GitHub stars) [uncertain]

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: Lindy: orchestrator with visual workflow builder, AI-first agent design with guided workflows (evolved from open-ended LLM agents to structured workflow-based approach); Relevance AI: multi_agent with orchestrator — supports agent teams where agents can delegate to each other (one finds info, another verifies, a third writes report); n8n: pipeline / graph_based — node-based visual workflow editor with AI agent nodes added as extension, event_driven triggers
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Lindy: Model-agnostic — supports GPT-4o, GPT-5, Claude 3.5/4/Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5, and others. Primary model is Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Lindy 2.0 default) with automatic model routing based on task complexity. Relevance AI: Model-agnostic — supports OpenAI (GPT series), Anthropic (Claude series), Google (Gemini series), Cohere, and DeepSeek-V3. Users select models per tool step. n8n: Model-agnostic via LangChain integration — supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama (local models), Hugging Face, and any model accessible via API. Users configure model per AI agent node.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Lindy: 5,000+ integrations via Pipedream partnership, 4,000+ web scrapers, native API connectors to CRM/email/scheduling/databases, Computer Use for browser automation beyond APIs. Relevance AI: 9,000+ tools, API connectors, custom code execution, pre-built templates, SDK for custom integrations, GitHub integration. n8n: 1,200+ native integrations (nodes), community nodes ecosystem (2,200+ publicly indexed), custom code nodes (JavaScript/Python), HTTP request node for any API, MCP Client/Server nodes for protocol-based integration.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: Lindy: Guided workflows with AI reasoning — agents follow structured workflow paths but can make decisions at branching points, supports conditional logic and human-in-the-loop approval steps. Relevance AI: LLM-driven reasoning within tool chains — agents use prompt chains with tool steps, multi-step coordination through agent delegation. n8n: Explicit graph-based planning — users define workflow logic visually, AI agent nodes use ReAct-style reasoning for autonomous steps within the broader workflow graph.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Lindy: Yes — supports 'agent swarms' (announced April 2025) where agents can duplicate themselves to perform hundreds of tasks in parallel, agents can trigger other agents in workflows. Relevance AI: Yes — core feature, supports building an 'AI workforce' as multi-agent systems where agents are organized into teams with defined roles, agents equipped with specific tools, agent-to-agent delegation within the platform. n8n: Limited native multi-agent — primarily single-agent workflows, but users can chain multiple AI agent nodes or trigger sub-workflows to simulate multi-agent behavior. No built-in agent team orchestration.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: Lindy: short_term (conversation context), semantic (persistent memory via vector embeddings — stores user preferences, previous interactions, task outcomes), episodic (can recall past interactions). Relevance AI: short_term (within tool execution), semantic (datasets stored in platform, vector search built-in), but tools are ephemeral by design — inputs/outputs not stored unless explicitly saved to datasets. n8n: short_term (workflow execution context), semantic (via vector store integrations — Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase, etc.), conversation memory via memory nodes (window buffer, summary, etc.).
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Lindy: Combines persistent memory (vector database embeddings) with working memory (current context), automatic retrieval of relevant past interactions and preferences. Relevance AI: Relies on LLM provider context windows, vector search for retrieval from stored datasets, prompt chain design manages context flow between steps. n8n: Configurable per AI agent — supports window buffer memory, summary memory, and vector store retrieval. Users explicitly design context flow through workflow nodes.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: Lindy: cloud (vector database for persistent memory, SaaS-managed); Relevance AI: cloud (SOC 2 Type II compliant platform storage, datasets persisted); n8n: database (workflow execution data in PostgreSQL/SQLite), vector_store (via integrations), file_system (self-hosted), cloud (n8n Cloud)
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Lindy: Context is a first-class concern — the platform automatically manages memory injection, retrieval of past interactions, and user preference loading into agent context. Prompt caching is used for cost optimization. Relevance AI: Moderate — context is managed through tool chain design and dataset connections, vector search provides contextual retrieval, but users must design context flow explicitly. n8n: User-managed — context engineering is done by the workflow builder through explicit memory node configuration, vector store connections, and data transformation nodes. No automatic context management.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Lindy: (1) Natural language agent creation — describe what you want and Lindy builds the agent, (2) Visual workflow builder with drag-and-drop, (3) 5,000+ integrations across email, CRM, scheduling, support, (4) Agent swarms for parallel task execution, (5) Computer Use for browser automation, (6) Lindy Build for app creation with automated testing, (7) Voice agent support for phone calls, (8) Pre-built templates for common use cases (meeting scheduling, email triage, customer support, sales follow-up), (9) Human-in-the-loop approval flows, (10) Knowledge base integration. Relevance AI: (1) No-code AI agent builder with visual interface, (2) Multi-agent system builder (AI Workforce), (3) Built-in vector search and RAG capabilities, (4) Tool Builder for custom integrations, (5) Prompt chain orchestration, (6) Bulk data processing with AI tools, (7) Agent templates for sales, marketing, research, (8) Auto-generated apps from tools, (9) Agent escalation protocols, (10) Dataset management with SOC 2 compliance. n8n: (1) Visual workflow automation with 1,200+ native integrations, (2) AI agent node with ReAct reasoning, (3) MCP Client/Server for protocol-based tool use, (4) Self-hosting option for full data control, (5) Custom code execution (JavaScript/Python), (6) Community template library (5,288+ AI workflows), (7) Git-based version control, (8) Webhook triggers and event-driven automation, (9) Sub-workflow composition, (10) Credential management with encryption.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Lindy: text, voice (phone calls), email, browser (Computer Use), file system, web scraping. Relevance AI: text, code, vision (image analysis), file processing (text/audio/image). n8n: text, code, file system, browser (via Selenium/Puppeteer nodes), email, webhooks, database.
capabilities.autonomy_level: Lindy: human_in_loop to fully_autonomous (configurable — supports approval steps, but agents can also run fully autonomously). Relevance AI: human_in_loop to supervised (agent escalation protocols, but also supports autonomous execution). n8n: human_in_loop to supervised (workflow-defined automation with optional manual triggers and approval gates).
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Lindy: 5,000+ integrations via Pipedream, 4,000+ web scrapers, pre-built templates. Relevance AI: 9,000+ tools, custom API connectors, SDK, pre-built templates. n8n: 1,200+ native nodes, 2,200+ community nodes, MCP protocol support, custom code nodes, HTTP request for any API.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Lindy: Not confirmed — Lindy's blog discusses MCP concepts but no official MCP client/server integration announced as of early 2026. Relevance AI: Not confirmed — no public documentation of MCP support found. n8n: Yes — native MCP support via MCP Server Trigger node (exposes n8n workflows as MCP tools) and MCP Client Tool node (connects to external MCP servers). Ships by default in recent versions. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Lindy: Not confirmed — no public A2A protocol support announced. Relevance AI: Not confirmed — no public A2A protocol support announced. n8n: Not confirmed — no native A2A protocol support found, though community nodes may provide this. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: None of the three platforms have documented support for AGENTS.md project instructions as of early 2026. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Lindy: Limited — primarily a self-contained SaaS platform, interoperability through API integrations and Pipedream. No direct framework-to-framework bridges. Relevance AI: Moderate — SDK available (Python), API access, can integrate with n8n via n8n's Relevance AI node. Self-contained but more developer-accessible. n8n: Strong — fair-code model enables deep integration, MCP support for protocol-based interop, REST API, webhook triggers, community nodes connect to virtually any service. Can orchestrate agents from other platforms (Lindy, Relevance AI, OpenAI, etc.) as workflow steps.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: Lindy: capability_based — role-based access controls (RBAC), enterprise SSO, agent-level permission configuration, API key management. Relevance AI: capability_based — role-based access control (RBAC), enterprise SSO, agent permissioning that mirrors real-world team structures. n8n: capability_based — role-based access control, credential management with encryption, workflow-level permissions, enterprise SSO.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Lindy: Configurable human-in-the-loop — agents can request approval before critical actions, fallback logic when agents reach limits, notification-based escalation. Relevance AI: Agent escalation protocols — agents can escalate to other agents or humans, configurable per agent role in the workforce hierarchy. n8n: Workflow-defined — users design explicit approval gates, manual trigger points, and error handling paths in the visual builder.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Lindy: Structured workflows constrain agent behavior to defined paths, reducing open-ended hallucination risk. Knowledge base grounding for factual responses. Guardrails for output validation. Relevance AI: Vector search grounding (built-in RAG), prompt chain design constrains outputs, tool-based verification steps. n8n: Depends on LLM provider settings, users can add validation nodes, output parsing, and conditional checks in workflows. No built-in hallucination detection.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Lindy: Yes — comprehensive audit logs, data encryption (AES-256), SOC 2 Type II compliant logging. Relevance AI: Yes — SOC 2 Type II compliant, dataset-level logging, agent execution tracking. n8n: Yes — workflow execution logs, audit logs (enterprise), version control via Git integration.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: Lindy: pre-approval (configurable approval steps before agent actions) and confidence_threshold (agents can be set to request approval for uncertain decisions). Relevance AI: pre-approval and post-review — agent escalation protocols allow routing to humans, multi-agent verification before output delivery. n8n: pre-approval — manual trigger nodes, approval gates in workflow design, human-in-the-loop at any workflow step.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Lindy: No external standards body governance — private company. Relevance AI: No external standards body governance — private company. n8n: Fair-code movement (faircode.io), n8n is listed as a fair-code pioneer. No formal standards body governance but aligns with open-source principles.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Lindy: Proprietary platform, does not implement or contribute to open protocols. Relevance AI: Proprietary platform, provides open SDK on GitHub but no formal protocol contributions. n8n: Implements MCP (Model Context Protocol) natively, contributes to the fair-code licensing model, source code publicly available under Sustainable Use License.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: Lindy: SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA (with BAA for healthcare), GDPR. Enterprise-grade compliance with AES-256 encryption in transit and at rest. Relevance AI: SOC 2 Type II, GDPR. Jurisdiction-specific hosting available. HIPAA compliance not confirmed. n8n: SOC 2 aligned (annual independent audits, SOC 2 report available to enterprise customers). Self-hosted option enables GDPR/HIPAA compliance by keeping data on-premises. HIPAA certification not explicitly provided by n8n Cloud. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: Lindy: cloud (managed SaaS only, no self-hosted option). Relevance AI: cloud (managed SaaS, jurisdiction-specific hosting available, no self-hosted option). n8n: cloud (n8n Cloud managed service), local (self-hosted via Docker/Docker Compose), hybrid (mix of cloud and self-hosted).
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: Lindy: serverless (managed SaaS scales automatically, credit-based usage). Relevance AI: serverless (managed SaaS, credit-based scaling). n8n: horizontal (self-hosted can scale across multiple instances with queue mode), serverless (n8n Cloud auto-scales), vertical (self-hosted single instance).
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Lindy: Credit-based — Free (400 credits/month), Pro ($49.99/month, 5,000 credits), Business ($299.99/month, 30,000 credits), Enterprise (custom). Cost per agent action depends on complexity and LLM model used. Relevance AI: Credit-based — Free (200 actions/month), Pro ($29/month), Team ($349/month), Enterprise (custom). Credits consumed per run: Free/Pro 4 credits, Team 3 credits, Enterprise 2 credits. n8n: Execution-based — Community (free self-hosted, unlimited executions), Starter (€24/month, 2,500 executions), Pro (€60/month, 10,000 executions), Enterprise (custom). Startup plan $400/month unlimited. Self-hosted free but requires server (~€5-20/month).
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Lindy: None (fully managed SaaS, web browser only). Relevance AI: None (fully managed SaaS, web browser only). n8n Cloud: None (managed). n8n self-hosted: Docker-capable server (minimum 1 vCPU, 2GB RAM for small workloads), PostgreSQL recommended for production, optional Redis for queue mode.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Lindy: Built-in execution monitoring dashboard, audit trails, agent performance tracking. No documented third-party observability tool integration (LangSmith, Langfuse, etc.). Relevance AI: Built-in agent execution tracking, dataset monitoring. No documented third-party observability integration. n8n: Built-in workflow execution logs and monitoring dashboard, error tracking with retry logic. Community integrations for external monitoring. Enterprise plan includes advanced execution logs. [uncertain]
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Lindy: Yes — workflow execution steps are visible in the builder UI, audit trail for each agent action. Relevance AI: Yes — tool chain execution is visible in the platform, step-by-step execution results. n8n: Yes — full workflow execution trace visible in the UI, each node's input/output is inspectable, execution history with detailed logs.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: Lindy: production_ready (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, enterprise customers, $5.1M ARR as of Oct 2024). Relevance AI: production_ready (SOC 2 Type II, Fortune 500 customers including Activision, 40,000+ agents created in Jan 2025 alone). n8n: enterprise_grade (SOC 2 aligned, 3,000+ enterprise customers, $2.5B valuation, 200,000+ active users, 723 employees).

adoption_and_market.github_stars: Lindy: N/A (proprietary, closed-source). Relevance AI: ~42 public repositories on GitHub, main SDK repo has modest stars (not a primary distribution channel). n8n: 89,000+ GitHub stars (one of the most-starred automation projects on GitHub).
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: Lindy: $5.1M ARR (Oct 2024), 5.5x growth in last 12 months, 70k waitlist signups at launch. Exact user count not publicly disclosed. ~37-person team. Relevance AI: 40,000+ agents created on the platform in January 2025 alone, clients range from scaleups to Fortune 500 (Activision, Qualified, SafetyCulture). n8n: 200,000+ active users, 3,000+ enterprise customers, 723 employees (Jan 2026), 5x YoY revenue growth, user base tripled in 3 months during 2025. $2.5B valuation.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Lindy: freemium (free tier + credit-based paid tiers). Relevance AI: freemium (free tier + credit-based paid tiers). n8n: open-source + freemium (free self-hosted Community edition + paid cloud/enterprise tiers based on executions).
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Lindy: Customer support automation, meeting scheduling, email triage, sales follow-up, lead qualification, voice agents for phone calls, CRM updates from meetings, recruiting workflows, content generation. Relevance AI: Sales outreach and prospecting, marketing campaign orchestration, research and summarization, data classification at scale, customer analytics, multi-agent research workflows, RAG-style assistants. n8n: IT/DevOps workflow automation, data pipeline orchestration, CRM synchronization, lead scoring with AI, customer support ticket routing, content generation pipelines, database synchronization, monitoring and alerting workflows.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Lindy: AI-first no-code leader for business automation — strongest when you want natural language agent creation with broad integrations and voice support. Competes with Zapier AI, Make, and other no-code platforms. Differentiates on AI-native design and agent swarms. Relevance AI: Strongest for multi-agent AI workforce with built-in vector search — best for teams building complex LLM-powered agents for research, sales, and data-heavy use cases. Competes with Lindy, crew.ai, and enterprise AI platforms. n8n: Strongest for developer-friendly automation with full control — open-source advantage for self-hosting and data sovereignty. Largest community and most integrations. Competes with Zapier, Make, and is increasingly positioned as an AI agent platform. Most mature and highest-valued of the three.

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: Lindy: Growing but smaller community — primarily users on the platform, Lindy blog with educational content, no large open-source community. Relevance AI: Moderate — active user base with 40k+ agents/month, GitHub SDK presence, documentation site, but smaller developer community than n8n. n8n: Very large — 89k+ GitHub stars, 200k+ active users, 2,200+ community-contributed nodes, active community forum, Discord, regular blog posts, 5,288+ community workflow templates.
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: Lindy: good (comprehensive blog content, template library, in-app guidance, Udemy course available). Relevance AI: good (dedicated docs site at relevanceai.com/docs, API reference, integration guides, open-source docs repo on GitHub). n8n: excellent (extensive documentation at docs.n8n.io, detailed node documentation for all 1,200+ integrations, tutorials, community templates, release notes, active blog).
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: Lindy: 5,000+ (via Pipedream partnership). Relevance AI: 9,000+ tools. n8n: 1,200+ native nodes + 2,200+ community nodes + MCP protocol support.
ecosystem_maturity.tutorial_availability: Lindy: good — blog tutorials, Udemy course ('Build AI Automations with Lindy'), template library with guided setup. Relevance AI: adequate — documentation site with guides, Analytics Vidhya tutorial, Skywork reviews with walkthroughs. n8n: excellent — extensive official tutorials, 5,288+ community workflow templates, numerous YouTube tutorials, blog guides, active community forum with solutions.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: Lindy: assistant to autonomous (configurable — from approval-required to fully independent operation). Relevance AI: assistant to autonomous (agents operate within defined tool chains, can escalate to humans or other agents). n8n: copilot to assistant (workflow-defined automation, AI agent nodes make decisions within scoped steps, humans design the overall flow).
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Lindy: Configurable approval steps in workflows — agents pause and notify humans when set up to do so, email/Slack notifications for handoff, fallback logic routes to humans on failure. Relevance AI: Agent escalation protocols — agents can escalate to other agents or to humans based on rules, permissioning mirrors real-world team hierarchies. n8n: Workflow-designed handoff — manual trigger nodes, wait nodes for human input, webhook-based approval flows, email/Slack notifications at any workflow step.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Lindy: Persistent memory captures user preferences and outcomes from past interactions, agents improve context over time through memory. No explicit reinforcement learning loop documented. Relevance AI: Dataset-level feedback — results can be stored and used to refine prompts and agent behavior. No explicit automated learning loop. n8n: No built-in feedback loop — users manually iterate on workflow design based on execution results. Workflow versioning via Git enables A/B testing of approaches.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: These three platforms represent the spectrum of no-code/low-code agent building for startups. Lindy is ideal for non-technical founders who need to quickly automate customer support, sales follow-up, scheduling, and voice interactions without any coding — it is the most 'AI-native' option with natural language agent creation. Relevance AI is best for startups that need to build AI-powered research, sales prospecting, or data analysis agents — its multi-agent architecture and built-in vector search make it powerful for LLM-heavy workflows. n8n is the best choice for technically-inclined teams that want maximum control, data sovereignty (self-hosting), and the ability to combine AI with complex business logic — its open-source model also means no vendor lock-in. For an M2 Entrepreneurship student: (1) Start with Lindy if you want to ship an AI-powered automation within hours with zero code, (2) Use Relevance AI if your startup is data-centric and needs AI agents that work with large datasets, (3) Use n8n if your team has a technical co-founder and you want to own your infrastructure. Key caution: all three platforms have credit/execution-based pricing that can scale up quickly — monitor usage closely. n8n's self-hosted free tier is the most cost-effective for bootstrapped startups.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: Buy (use these platforms) when: you need agent automation quickly without hiring AI engineers, your use case fits common patterns (support, sales, scheduling), and you are testing product-market fit. Build custom when: you need proprietary AI logic, extreme customization, or your use case requires capabilities these platforms do not support. Cost comparison: Lindy Pro at $50/month or n8n self-hosted at ~€10/month is far cheaper than hiring an AI engineer ($100k+/year). Relevance AI Team at $349/month may be justified if multi-agent research is core to your business. n8n offers the best 'build-buy hybrid' — self-host for free, customize with code, but use the visual builder for speed.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy, AI Canvas) and Session 4 (AI business models & strategy — tool selection for scaling). Also relevant to Session 2 (No-code tools and prompt engineering).

confidence.data_quality: Medium-High — information sourced from official product pages, reputable tech publications (TechCrunch, SmartCompany), comparison reviews, and community forums. Pricing and feature details confirmed across multiple sources. Some specific version numbers and MCP/A2A support details could not be fully verified.
confidence.cross_reference: Lindy features/pricing confirmed via lindy.ai, max-productive.ai, skywork.ai, and multiple comparison articles. Relevance AI confirmed via relevanceai.com, Bessemer VP blog, SmartCompany, G2. n8n confirmed via n8n.io, TechCrunch (Series B/C), Wikipedia, GitHub repository, community docs. Comparison data from Lindy blog, techraisal.com, nuvi.dev, and aimultiple.com.
confidence.caveats: This is a rapidly evolving space — all three platforms ship frequent updates. Pricing tiers and credit amounts may change. n8n's valuation jumped from €250M (March 2025) to $2.5B (October 2025) in seven months, indicating explosive growth and potential pricing model changes. Lindy is the youngest platform and features like agent swarms (April 2025) are relatively new. Relevance AI's pivot from data platform to AI workforce is recent. MCP and A2A protocol support across these platforms is still emerging and may change significantly in 2026. Integration counts (5,000+, 9,000+, 1,200+) are self-reported and may count differently across platforms.
